inputs.base_revenue_note: TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY2025 13,951.7 + H1-2026 7,268.7 - H1-2025 6,872.4. FY ends 31 December; the TTM base is used so that Y1 flows begin where the 2026-06-30 balance sheet ends.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted; H1-2026 net income 577.1 / diluted EPS 7.03 = 82.1M weighted diluted, Q2-2026 299.1 / 3.66 = 81.7M; period-end basic ~81.5M after $452M H1 buybacks plus ~0.5M dilutive overhang -> 82.0M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: TTM to 2026-06-30: OCF 1,638.4 (1,640.5 + 637.0 - 639.1) less capex 483.2 (434.5 + 252.6 - 203.9). Reported FCF is after cash interest (~$230M/yr) and before acquisition spend; the component build below is unlevered (EBIT x (1-t)) so Y1 owner FCF is not directly comparable to this levered figure. FY2026 company FCF guidance is $1.24-1.36B.
inputs.sbc_source: XBRL cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation (TTM 125.8 + 66.6 - 66.9 = 125.5) plus PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation (TTM 31.9 + 46.1 - 29.0 = 49.0) summed, because Labcorp publishes no combined equity-award figure (SBC is not excluded from its adjusted metrics).
inputs.buyback_note: TTM repurchases 450.0 (FY2025) + 451.8 (H1-2026) - 200.0 (H1-2025). The flat count is funded: buybacks run at ~4x the SBC charge.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.9 for a defensive diagnostics duopolist -> cost of equity ~8.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.8% (BBB, recent issuance), ~4.5% after tax. Net debt 5.7B against ~25B market cap -> ~19% debt weight. WACC ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, through the scenario weights.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A): operating lease cost sits inside GAAP operating expense and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path; finance leases are immaterial; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. No lease_cost_pct_path.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (<$20M); no adjustment.
inputs.ebitda_anchor_note: TTM GAAP EBITDA (operating income + D&A) = 2,192.9 = 15.3% of revenue, after SBC (0.9%) and after ~2pp of amortisation-excluded restructuring, acquisition and special items. Pre-SBC EBITDA = 16.2% on a pure GAAP basis; adjusted (company) basis would be ~18.5%. The base Y1 margin of 17.2% adds back SBC and roughly half of the special items, treating the other ~1pp as a recurring cost of a serial acquirer (13+ outreach deals 2025-26).
inputs.capex_note: Maintenance capex TTM 483.2 = 3.4% of revenue. Guided revenue growth (5-8% CAGR) includes ~1-1.5pp per year from outreach-lab acquisitions, which are not in capex. To avoid taking acquired growth for free, capex_pct carries an explicit acquisition charge: base ~1.6pp (~$230-260M/yr, roughly 1.5x acquired revenue), bull ~1.9pp, bear ~0.8pp as the deal cadence slows.
inputs.tax_note: GAAP effective rate ~24%. FY2025 cash taxes were 171.1 on ~1.15B pretax (~15%) and FY2024 215.4 (~22%); the FY2025 figure is timing. Cash tax is applied to EBIT after full GAAP D&A (acquired intangibles from asset-purchase outreach deals are tax-deductible) and ramps 21% -> 24%.
inputs.working_capital_note: Receivables ~15% of revenue less payables/accruals leave net operating working capital ~8% of revenue, so growth consumes cash: wc_capture_pct = -8 (negative capture on the revenue CHANGE).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (make build-dcf), 10-year horizon because the margin path, cash-tax ramp and M&A taper all run past year 5. Labcorp is a mature, profitable US operating company (clinical lab testing duopolist with Quest; Diagnostics ~76% / Biopharma Laboratory Services ~24%) - not a bank, REIT, LIC or distressed shell, so the routing table sends it to owner-fcf.md; owner-fcf-adaptations.md does not apply (USD filer and quote, no NCI, operating leases already in opex). First valuation of this ticker: no memory entry, no prior DCF. SBC is expensed and the share count held flat; buybacks fund the flat count. Interest income is zero (net debt of 5.7B). Historical CAGRs are distorted by the FY2020-22 COVID-testing windfall and the June-2023 Fortrea spin-off; growth is anchored to guidance instead (see historical_growth.notes). Price is the 2026-10-01 regular close, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2026 guidance (revenue +5.4-6.3%) and the September-2026 Investor Day 2026-2029 outlook (5-8% revenue CAGR), taken at the low end; historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward anchor (see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-5.1% 3yr) diverges from revenue CAGR (+5.6% 3yr) by far more than 30%, and EPS/FCF CAGRs are negative. All three- and five-year windows start inside the COVID-testing windfall (FY2020-22 revenue 13.1-14.0B with ~$1-3B of COVID testing) and straddle the June-2023 Fortrea spin-off (~$1.5B+ of equity distributed, ~$3B of CRO revenue removed; FY2022 shown restated for discontinued ops). None of these CAGRs describe the current business.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC less equity-award taxes): FY2025 1,048.3 vs FY2022 1,359.2 vs FY2020 ~1,608. Owner-FCF CAGR is ~0.7pp below the reported-FCF CAGR over 3 years, so SBC is not growing faster than cash flow; SBC has been flat at ~0.9% of revenue since FY2019. The pre-COVID FY2015-FY2019 window (post-Covance, pre-pandemic) gives revenue 7.4% and equity 11.5% including M&A, a better guide to the normal franchise than the headline 3/5-year figures.

base.narrative: Low end of the 2026-2029 outlook: ~5.5% growth through 2028 (4-4.5% organic plus ~1pp acquired) tapering to 2.5%; ~90bps of pre-SBC EBITDA expansion by Y4 (guidance 75-150bps op-margin expansion); PAMA cuts land at a moderated level, as management has embedded; M&A spend charged at ~1.6% of revenue tapering to 0.6% as the outreach runway thins.

bull.narrative: Midpoint of the 5-8% outlook: ACLA litigation or CMS revision moderates the 2027-29 PAMA cuts, Central Labs keeps BLS at 6-7%, specialty mix shift and outreach consolidation deliver the top of the 75-150bps margin band (~180bps pre-SBC EBITDA by Y5); M&A cadence stays at 13+ deals/yr, charged at ~1.9% of revenue.

bear.narrative: CMS finalises the preliminary 2027-2029 CLFS rates at or near the proposed magnitude: Medicare-paid routine testing takes ~1-1.5pp off Dx revenue growth each year for three years, Quest price competition stops commercial payers from backfilling, and a biotech-funding downturn flattens BLS. Growth drops to 2-2.5%, pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses ~120bps to 16.0% before a partial recovery, and the outreach M&A engine slows (acquisition charge ~0.8pp). The business remains solidly cash-generative - this is a reimbursement-reset case, not a solvency case.

scenario_narratives.base: Labcorp executes at the low end of its September-2026 Investor Day framework: enterprise revenue grows ~5.5-5.7% in the next two years (FY2026 guidance 5.4-6.3%; ~4-4.5% organic plus ~1pp from outreach-lab acquisitions), decelerating to 2.5% by year 9. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin expands ~90bps to 18.1% by year 4 on specialty/esoteric mix shift and Central Labs utilisation, consistent with guided 75-150bps of adjusted operating-margin expansion, then holds. PAMA cuts for 2027-2029 land at a moderated level - management says the anticipated pressure is already inside the outlook. Cash tax ramps 21% to 24%; D&A drifts from 4.8% to 4.6% as acquired intangibles roll off; capex carries a ~1.6pp acquisition charge that tapers to 0.6pp. SBC stays ~1.2% of revenue including net-share-settlement taxes. WACC 8%, terminal growth 2.5%, terminal cap 18x.
scenario_narratives.bull: PAMA relief is the swing: ACLA litigation or a CMS data-methodology revision moderates the 2027-29 cuts, so Dx grows 5.5-6% organically plus M&A while BLS Central Labs sustains 6-7% on resilient biopharma trial demand. Revenue compounds at ~6.5% through 2028 (the midpoint of the 5-8% outlook), and the margin program reaches the top of the band (~180bps of pre-SBC EBITDA expansion to 19.0% by year 5). The outreach consolidation runway (Labcorp + Quest hold only ~25% of US tests) supports a 13+ deal/yr cadence, charged at ~1.9% of revenue. Same WACC and terminal assumptions as base.
scenario_narratives.bear: CMS finalises the 2027-2029 CLFS rates near the preliminary proposal and the ACLA challenge fails. Medicare routine-test reimbursement falls each year for three years, taking 1-1.5pp off Dx growth; duopoly price competition with Quest prevents commercial repricing; a biotech funding downturn flattens BLS bookings. Revenue growth falls to 2-2.5% from year 2, pre-SBC EBITDA margin compresses ~120bps to 16.0% by year 4 before a partial recovery to 16.2%, and management slows the M&A engine (capex charge drops to ~3.6-4.4%). Terminal growth 2.0%. The company still generates ~$1.0B+ of unlevered owner FCF - the bear case is a lower-growth, lower-margin reset, not a distress case, which is why WACC is not raised.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the CMS preliminary 2027-2029 PAMA rates are a live, already-published single-regulator threat to the largest revenue pool, and the outcome is binary on litigation/rulemaking rather than on execution. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs PAMA relief, top-of-band margin expansion and a sustained 13+ deal/yr cadence to all land together. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was raised twice and the long-term outlook was reaffirmed after the PAMA release, so the central case is management's low end.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Labcorp is valued as a mature, defensive cash compounder on fully SBC-expensed unlevered owner FCF, with the growth that outreach acquisitions buy charged against the flows as an explicit acquisition line rather than taken for free. The forward margin is built from components anchored to TTM Jun-2026 GAAP EBITDA plus SBC and half of the special items, and expands only within management's guided 75-150bps band. Historical CAGRs are reported but deliberately not used as the growth anchor because every multi-year window is distorted by COVID testing and the Fortrea spin. Risk is charged once, through 25/50/25 scenario weights, at a single 8% USD WACC; the 18x terminal cap sits just under Gordon at 8%/2.5% and well under today's ~24x EV/owner-FCF, so no multiple expansion is assumed.
key_risks_to_valuation: CMS 2027-2029 PAMA Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule cuts finalised at the preliminary magnitude (bear case) - Medicare routine testing reimbursement is set by a single regulator
Duopoly price competition with Quest Diagnostics for payer networks and hospital outreach contracts capping commercial pricing
Acquired-growth accounting: if outreach deals cost materially more than ~1.5x acquired revenue, the 1.6pp acquisition charge understates the cash cost of the guided growth
Biopharma funding cycle flattening BLS/Central Labs bookings (24% of revenue)
Integration risk across 13+ small, geographically dispersed outreach acquisitions per year
Special items (restructuring, acquisition costs, AMCA litigation) treated as ~half recurring; if they are fully recurring the EBITDA anchor is ~1pp too high
Terminal value is ~65-75% of enterprise value; a 1pp move in WACC moves the base value by roughly 15-20%
